module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Serre's uniformity conjecture over the rationals

Is there a bound $C$, independent of the non-CM elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$, such that
the Galois action on $E[p]$ is surjective onto $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ for every
prime $p > C$? This is the $\mathbb{Q}$ case of Serre's question [Ser72], recalled in
the introduction of [Lem17].

We express surjectivity without choosing a basis: every additive automorphism of $E[p]$
must be induced by an element of $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$. For prime $p$, these automorphisms are
exactly the $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear automorphisms. The non-CM condition uses the classification
of rational CM $j$-invariants.

*References:*
- [Ser72] J.-P. Serre, *Propriétés galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes
  elliptiques*. Inventiones Mathematicae 15 (1972), 259–331.
  https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01405086
- [Lem17] P. Lemos, *Serre's uniformity conjecture for elliptic curves with rational
  cyclic isogenies*, introduction. https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.01985
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace SerreUniformity

/--
The thirteen rational CM $j$-invariants.
-/
def cmJInvariants : Finset ℚ :=
  {0, 1728, -3375, 8000, -32768, 54000, 287496, -884736,
    -12288000, 16581375, -884736000, -147197952000, -262537412640768000}

open scoped Classical in
/--
Every additive automorphism of $E[p]$ is induced by a Galois automorphism.
For elliptic $E$ and prime $p$, this means that the mod-$p$ representation is surjective.
-/
def HasFullTorsionAction (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  let T := AddSubgroup.torsionBy (E.baseChange (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)).toAffine.Point (p : ℤ)
  ∀ f : T ≃+ T, ∃ σ : AlgebraicClosure ℚ ≃ₐ[ℚ] AlgebraicClosure ℚ,
    ∀ P : T, WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.map (W' := E) σ.toAlgHom P.val = (f P).val

/--
**Serre's uniformity question over $\mathbb{Q}$** [Ser72, Lem17]: is there a bound
$C$ such that every non-CM elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has surjective mod-$p$
Galois representation for every prime $p > C$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem serre_uniformity :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic], E.j ∉ cmJInvariants →
        ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → C < p → HasFullTorsionAction E p := by
  sorry

/--
**Serre's uniformity conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$, explicit form**: the bound $C = 37$
works, i.e. every non-CM elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has surjective mod-$p$ Galois
representation for every prime $p > 37$. From the introduction of [Lem17]: "This conjecture
remains open today, but, over the last forty years, there has been a lot of progress towards
a proof for $K = \mathbb{Q}$ — it is believed that, in this case, $p_K = 37$."
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem serre_uniformity.variants.bound_37 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic], E.j ∉ cmJInvariants →
        ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → 37 < p → HasFullTorsionAction E p := by
  sorry

end SerreUniformity

reformulations.difference: Surjectivity onto GL₂(F_p) is expressed without choosing a basis: every additive automorphism of the p-torsion must be induced by one rational Galois automorphism, simultaneously on all torsion points.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For elliptic E/ℚ and prime p, E[p](ℚ̄) is a two-dimensional F_p-vector space. Every additive automorphism is F_p-linear, since scalar multiplication is repeated addition. Choosing a basis identifies this automorphism group with GL₂(F_p). Mathlib's Point includes the point at infinity, torsionBy selects precisely the points killed by p, and Point.map applies the field automorphism to coordinates. Thus the quantified condition is exactly surjectivity of the mod-p representation. Scratch Lean proofs establish the additive-versus-ZMod-linear equivalence and equivalence to surjectivity onto additive automorphisms; the rank-two identification was checked mathematically, not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Both conjectures express geometric non-CM by excluding this finite set of rational j-invariants, rather than requiring End over ℚ̄ to equal ℤ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The thirteen imaginary quadratic orders of class number one give exactly the thirteen rational CM j-invariants. The complete list in SageMath's CM documentation agrees with the Lean list, including signs and the nonmaximal-order cases. CM depends only on the geometric isomorphism class, which is determined by j. Consequently, for elliptic curves over ℚ, exclusion from this set is equivalent to the source's non-CM hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: The existential bound C is any natural number, whereas Lemos phrases the bound p_K as a prime number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If a natural bound C works, choose a prime q ≥ C. Every prime p > q also exceeds C, so q works as a prime bound. Conversely, a prime bound is a natural bound. The exact equivalence for the file's uniformly quantified condition was proved in /workspace/review/action.lean.

J.-P. Serre, Propriétés galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes elliptiques: https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01405086 (publisher metadata read; full text unavailable).
Serre article bibliographic record and archival link: https://eudml.org/doc/142133

review.notes: All four mathematical declarations were checked. Lemos's introduction poses the general uniformity question and explicitly discusses the ℚ-case bound 37; its proved theorem additionally assumes a rational cyclic isogeny, so it does not settle either declaration here. Lean checks passed for the CM list's cardinality, a concrete elliptic non-CM example, exclusion of the singular zero equation, torsion boundary cases, and the action equivalences. Serre's original full text was inaccessible via the publisher and archival links; the cited Lemos introduction supplied precise statements of both questions. No repository files were modified.
